newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower after Wall Street slide.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower after Wall Street slide.

text.p: French stocks retreated at the open of trading on the Paris bourse on Friday following an overnight slide on Wall Street, with almost every single stock in the CAC-40 leading share index turning downwards in early exchanges.

Dealers said the market, already consolidating for two days, had been expected to ease further on Friday, monthly settlement day, but that it could recover some ground once the initial reaction to Wall Street's fall subsided.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 16.13 points or 0.63 percent at 2,559,11 at 0926 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down 18.0 at 2564.0
"We're going to retreat a little but probably pull back at the end of the day," said one dealer.
Shares in leisure group Club Mediterranee were suspended pending a statement from the group whose board was meeting on Friday.
The newspaper La Tribune said in its Friday edition that the resort group could end the 1996 financial year in the red and could announce important strategic and management measures.
Its shares were hit in October after a company warning that pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit for the second half of 1995/96 would be similar to the year-earlier level.
Oil company Elf underperformed the market after reporting 1996 consolidated turnover of 232.71 billion francs, compared with 208.29 billion francs.
Michelin's stock was up slightly. The company said it planned to eliminate 1,445 posts through early retirements, transfers and other measures but hoped to avoid outright layoffs.

Insurer AGF rose strongly, gaining 3.26 percent. German bank Merck, Finck & Co said the time may be right for German insurer Allianz AG Holding to take over AGF, given the French group's value, expected earnings development and share price.
